steps.what: Write technical reports from held engineering project records.

loop.input: a record id and one sentence from that record
loop.output: a sentence kept only when that record states it
loop.check: The sentence cites a record id and the record text contains it.
loop.stop: Stop when there is no record id, or the record does not state the sentence. The engineer writes that part.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot tell which sentence is absent from the held engineering record, so it would present a claim the record does not state.

steps.what: Accept technical reports or proposals and write any missing sentence.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store keeps a sentence in a technical report or proposal only when a held engineering record states it, and every number must trace to that record. The fuel cell engineer writes any missing sentence and accepts the text. Only that accepted version is filed. It is not sent. A sentence the record does not state is left for the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: A proposal repeated a number that was not in the test record it cited.
tasks.enabler_now: A held record can supply a sentence it actually states. The report still has to be accepted.
tasks.still_hard: A proposal claim the record does not state still has to be written by the engineer, or left out.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer writes the missing sentences and accepts the report. A quoted sentence is not the report.
tasks.altitude: The report is still accepted by the engineer before it is filed. Quoted record text is only a draft, and the file is not a send.

reach.task: Read a report the fuel cell engineer has accepted.
reach.learn: A quoted test sentence is not the proposal.

evidence.claim: A sentence may be kept only when a record the company already holds states it, and a number must trace to that record.
Filing the report before the engineer accepts that version would store sentences nobody accepted. The file is not a send.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A fuel cell engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the experiment, and a draft is not the accepted design.
Fields: A record id and the sentence on that record. A number with no record id is not kept. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the fuel cell engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read the engineering record from the document store before writing the report.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the fuel cell engineer.
unknowns: Whether proposals and test reports are allowed to cite the same record ids.
research_questions: Which record types may be quoted into a technical report or proposal?

already_counted.description: Writing missing sentences and accepting the report stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop report sentences whose source record has been replaced.

approvals.approved_version: report version and the record ids it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still writes any sentence the record does not state and still accepts the report or proposal. The draft may repeat only a sentence a held record states, every number must trace to a record, and only that accepted version is filed. It is not sent. A silent record saves none of the writing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the stored parameters for this fuel cell or motor.
Simulate or model fuel cell, motor, or system information.

tasks.design: The {DATA_PLATFORM} shows parameters already stored for this fuel cell, motor, or system. The fuel cell engineer simulates and interprets the result. Solver runtime is not counted, and a result stored for other conditions is not this prediction. A missing boundary value stops the screen and the engineer sets it.
tasks.previous_blocker: A result from another temperature was shown as the prediction for this case.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored parameters can be opened. The simulation and the interpretation still belong to the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A case the stored parameters do not describe still has to be set up by the engineer.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer runs and interprets the simulation. A stored result from other conditions is not this one.
tasks.altitude: Simulation judgement stays with the engineer. Solver runtime is not treated as saved labour.

reach.task: Use a simulation case the fuel cell engineer has interpreted.
reach.learn: A stored result from other conditions is not this prediction.

evidence.claim: Opening stored parameters is a lookup. It does not simulate the cell, the motor, or the system.
A solver can finish and still be wrong. Solver runtime is not the engineer's labour, and executable is not the same as correct.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A fuel cell engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the experiment, and a draft is not the accepted design.

Fields: The case id and the boundary parameters already stored for this case. A result stored for another case is not shown as this prediction. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the fuel cell engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the parameters for this case. Do not reuse a result whose conditions differ.
unknowns: Whether motor cases and fuel cell cases share one parameter record.
research_questions: Who confirms that a stored result belongs to this case's conditions?

already_counted.description: Running and interpreting the simulation stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop parameter sets whose case record has been withdrawn.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still simulates the cell, motor, or system and still interprets the result. Only opening parameters already stored for this case is removed. Solver runtime is not counted, and a result from other conditions saves none of the judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the stored duty for this stack or subsystem.
Design fuel cell systems, stacks, or electric traction motors.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the duty already stored for this system, stack, or component. The fuel cell engineer designs the system, the stack, the assembly, or the traction motor and power electronics. The duty is not the design. Only the design the engineer accepts is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: A stack design was filed against a duty that belonged to a different vehicle.
tasks.enabler_now: The stored duty can be opened. The design still has to be drawn by the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A load the duty does not state still has to be designed for by the engineer, or refused.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer designs the system. The duty is the requirement already stored.
tasks.altitude: The design stays with the engineer. It is filed only after that version is accepted.

reach.task: Use a system design the fuel cell engineer has accepted.
reach.learn: A duty statement is not the design.

evidence.claim: Opening a stored duty is a lookup. It does not design a system, a stack, a motor, or the power electronics.
Filing a design before the engineer accepts that version would store a drawing nobody made.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A fuel cell engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the experiment, and a draft is not the accepted design.
Fields: The duty id already stored. The design geometry is not added by the screen. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the fuel cell engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the duty in the document store before starting the design.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the fuel cell engineer.
unknowns: Whether traction motors and power electronics share one duty record.
research_questions: Who confirms the duty is the one for this vehicle?

already_counted.description: Designing the system stays with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop duties whose vehicle record has been withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: duty id and the design version the engineer accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still designs the system, stack, assembly, motor, or power electronics. Only opening a duty that was already stored, and filing the design already accepted, is removed. A duty with no id saves none of the design.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show stored interfaces for this fuel cell vehicle.
Identify integration challenges for these fuel cell vehicles.
File the accepted integration challenge note.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows interfaces already stored for this fuel cell vehicle. The fuel cell engineer identifies the integration challenges. The interface list is not the challenge. Only the challenge note the engineer accepts is filed, and a vehicle with no interface record is left with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: An interface list was filed as the challenge list, and the actual clash was still undescribed.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored interfaces can be opened. The challenges still have to be identified by the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A clash the interface list does not show still has to be named by the engineer.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer identifies the challenge. The interface list is the record already stored.
tasks.altitude: Naming the challenge stays with the engineer. The note is filed only after that version is accepted.

reach.task: Read a challenge note the fuel cell engineer has accepted.
reach.learn: An interface list is not the challenge.

evidence.claim: Opening stored interfaces is a lookup. It does not identify or define an integration challenge.
Filing a challenge note before the engineer accepts that version would store a problem nobody named.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A fuel cell engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the experiment, and a draft is not the accepted design.

Fields: The vehicle id and the interface ids already stored. The challenge text is not added by the screen. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the fuel cell engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the interface list in the document store before writing the challenge note.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the fuel cell engineer.
unknowns: Whether vehicle interfaces and system interfaces share one list.
research_questions: Who adds an interface to the vehicle record?

already_counted.description: Identifying the challenges stays with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop interface rows whose vehicle record has been withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: vehicle id, interface ids, and the challenge sentence the engineer accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still identifies the integration challenges. Only opening interfaces already stored, and filing the challenge note already accepted, is removed. The interface list saves none of that judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fuel cell engineer still writes the report, still interprets the simulation, still designs the system, and still names the integration challenge. A stored sentence can be kept. It is not the report.
reach: Project managers read an accepted report, and this job learns a quoted test record is not the report.
Vehicle engineers read an accepted challenge note, and this job learns an interface list is not the challenge.
skills_to_grow: Keep a report sentence only when the held record states it, and write the rest.
Treat a simulation result from other conditions as a different case.
Name an integration challenge from the vehicle, not from the interface list alone.
role.ambitious_version: Reports, simulation judgement, system design, and integration challenges stay with the engineer. Stored records only supply what they already state.
